GEModelR is an R package with compiled native code. Keep changes focused on
the owning subsystem, preserve the public `GEModel` workflow, and support
each behavioral change with small, deterministic evidence.

## Set up and run focused checks

From the package root, install the local source to compile its native code.
Run the narrowest relevant testthat group while iterating, then build and
check the source archive so validation covers the package users install.

```sh
R CMD INSTALL .
Rscript --vanilla -e 'testthat::test_local(filter = "public-solver-contract")'
R CMD build .
R CMD check --no-manual GEModelR_0.1.0.tar.gz
```

For solver changes, include the applicable sparse-core, backend, numerical
acceptance, cleanup, or diagnostics coverage. Use the small fixtures and
helpers under `tests/testthat/`; do not use a legacy result as the numerical
authority for sparse behavior. The external full-scale benchmark is a
separate workflow and is not part of ordinary tests, package checks, or site
builds.

## Native code and generated wrappers

Keep native implementations in the focused files under `src/` and their R
capability/adaptor code in the matching sparse modules. If an Rcpp
`// [[Rcpp::export]]` declaration changes, regenerate both wrapper files from
the package root:

```r
Rcpp::compileAttributes()
```

`R/RcppExports.R` and `src/RcppExports.cpp` are generated outputs; do not
hand-edit them. Rebuild or install the package after regeneration so symbol
registration, arities, and the compiled library are checked together.

The native CI matrix exercises serial builds on Linux, macOS, and Windows,
plus OpenMP builds on Linux and Windows. It verifies both the minimum and
current Matrix compatibility endpoints across selected R releases. Keep
serial behavior correct and deterministic. Request multiple native threads
only when the installed build reports OpenMP support; a serial build must
reject an unsupported thread request clearly.

## Numerical and review expectations

Solver changes should preserve the candidate acceptance boundary: check
shape and finiteness, recompute the true residual, and apply a sparse result
only after it passes. Keep memory and allocation behavior observable through
the supported diagnostics, and release solve-scoped native resources on
both success and failure. Add or update a focused regression test when a
change affects these contracts.

Contributions are submitted through pull requests. Describe the behavior
change, the relevant tests and package checks, and any minimal redistributable
fixture needed to reproduce it. The governance process requires applicable
CI checks before merge and does not use direct, unreviewed release changes.

## Keep data private and builds reproducible

Commit only small, redistributable examples and fixtures. Never add
proprietary TABLO or HAR inputs, credentials, full-scale model outputs, or
large benchmark scratch files to the repository. Full-scale benchmark runs
must use locally supplied inputs outside the package and site build; submit
only approved, redacted summaries when a benchmark result is part of a
review.
